provider: Title Insurance Rate Service Association of New York, Inc. (TIRSA) — Title Insurance Rate Manual for New York State (REGULATORY/RATING-BUREAU-UNIFORM, not provider-set)
sourceUrl: https://ratecalculator.fnf.com/Documents/TIRSA%20Rate%20Manual%20Appvd%20June%2010%202024%20Effective%20Oct%201%202024.pdf (Seventh Revision, approved by the NY DFS Superintendent June 10, 2024, effective October 1, 2024); vintage confirmed current as of retrieval via https://tirsa.org/rate-manual/, which states the current manual 'replaces and supersedes previous versions'
asOf: Seventh Revision, DFS-approved 06/10/2024, effective 10/01/2024 -- current vintage as of retrieval 2026-07-22

settlementFee.note: TIRSA sets NY title insurance PREMIUM rates uniformly for every member insurer/agent statewide (owner's and loan policy rates keyed to liability amount) under the Insurance Law of the State of New York -- this is the regulatory backbone, not a market signal. TIRSA's Manual governs the insurance premium itself; it does NOT set settlement/closing, doc prep, courier, wire, or notary fees, which are separately, competitively priced by the title agency/attorney handling the closing. A separate DFS regulation, 11 NYCRR Part 228 ('Insurance Regulation 208'), attempted in 2017-2019 to cap 'ancillary or other discretionary fees' (Patriot search, bankruptcy search, municipal/departmental searches, recording charges) at 200% of the agency's own out-of-pocket cost, and to restrict payments to closers -- but Part 228's ancillary-fee-ceiling and closer-payment provisions were ANNULLED by an Article 78 court decision effective January 15, 2019 (New York State Land Title Association, Inc. v. NYS DFS), so titled agencies/agents are NOT currently required to comply with those ceilings. The practical effect: even the one NY regulatory attempt to cap non-premium service fees has been struck down, leaving settlement/service-fee pricing fully market-set statewide -- exactly the unregulated territory this survey targets.
settlementFee.premiumOnly: Not itemized in this survey (see PA.md/other rating-bureau states' entries for representative promulgated-premium-table detail; NY's premium schedule is analogous in structure -- liability-tiered Sale/Non-Sale-style rates set once for all TIRSA members). This entry exists to document the regulatory reference point, not to duplicate the premium table.

itemizedFees.searchExam: Search/exam costs when performed by the title agent are part of the TIRSA-regulated premium calculation in some circumstances but settlement/closing services are not covered by the Manual
itemizedFees.cpl: CPL fees are set by TIRSA-member insurers' own bulletins, not standardized within the Manual itself; not itemized in this survey

other.name: 11 NYCRR Part 228 ancillary-fee ceiling (Patriot/bankruptcy/municipal search fees capped at 200% of cost)
other.amount: Judicially ANNULLED effective 01/15/2019 -- not currently enforceable

bundlingNotes: NY is a rating-bureau-uniform PREMIUM state (TIRSA), but unlike PA's TIRBOP, TIRSA's all-inclusive rate concept does not extend to bundling settlement/closing services into the regulated premium -- NY closings are attorney-run (buyer's and seller's attorneys both customarily attend), and the title agency's settlement/closing fee, doc prep, courier, wire, and notary fees are separately, competitively priced by whichever title agency and/or attorney is retained. The 2019 annulment of Part 228's ancillary-fee ceiling further confirms these categories are market-set, not regulator-set, in New York.
transactionContext: Applies uniformly to Owner's and Loan policy premiums statewide, all counties, all TIRSA-member insurers/agents. Does not govern settlement/closing fees, which is why this survey's remaining entries are all provider-published service-fee schedules.

bundlingNotes: The single richest multi-metro data point found this session: Judicial Title publishes an explicit three-way regional split for its Full Municipal Search -- Westchester/Putnam/Orange/Dutchess/Rockland/'Upstate' vs. NYC Boroughs vs. Nassau & Suffolk -- directly covering three of the task brief's target metros (Westchester/Hudson Valley, NYC, Long Island) in one schedule, with the Boroughs price ($475-$545) running highest, consistent with NYC's added ACRIS-recording complexity. Its flat $1,500 Settlement Charge is 3x Tier One's $500 residential settlement fee, the widest headline-settlement-fee spread found this session (see NY.md saturation reasoning) -- plausibly reflecting different scopes of service (full-service escrow/settlement administration vs. a narrower settlement-attendance fee) rather than a like-for-like comparison.
transactionContext: Statewide NY; the Full Municipal Search table is explicitly broken out by residential vs. commercial and by the three metro regions above. Settlement Charge and other named charges are flat, not metro-differentiated on this page.
